clue.text: Cordelia represented by unknown artist

indicators.note: the name is represented in a new form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter Cordelia painted by some anonymous artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is the anagram signal. Eugène Delacroix was the French Romantic painter of Liberty Leading the People.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Delacroix was a leading French Romantic painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Play doctor and nurse? That's not hard

indicators.note: not hard tells us the pencil abbreviation for hard is dropped from the nurse word

parts.note: an amah is a nursemaid in East and South Asia
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hospital drama about doctors and nurses is an easy watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not hard' drops the pencil-grade letter for hard. An amah is a nursemaid in East and South Asia, a word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of theatre, which is the core sense of a stage work of this kind.

clue.text: Novel Ales 'n' Wagnerites must be an Inspector Morse book

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters that follow take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Beer and Wagner fans are a fitting backdrop for Colin Dexter's opera-loving, ale-drinking detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' rearranges the fifteen letters of ALES N WAGNERITES. Morse famously loved real ale and Wagner, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Last Seen Wearing is the second of Colin Dexter's Inspector Morse detective novels, published in 1976.

clue.text: Politeness of Spanish parliament about universal end to poverty

indicators.note: the parliament word goes about, or around, the letter for universal

parts.note: the Cortes is the Spanish parliament
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: the end of the word poverty is its final letter

explanation.surface: Madrid's parliament is said to have shown civility on the topic of ending poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtesy is a synonym of politeness: both mean considerate, well-mannered behaviour toward others.

clue.text: Going away? Blooming limit

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
a bound is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether the flowering has hit its limit and is fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Outbound describes travel heading away from a place, as in an outbound flight leaving the airport.

clue.text: Cross queen twice almost succeeded as ruler after Darius

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of that doubled run is dropped
twice means the cross-and-queen pair is written two times over

parts.note: a cross is the shape of the letter X
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: An irate queen, nearly crossed twice, followed the Persian king to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives XERXER; 'almost' drops its last R, leaving XERXE, then S. Xerxes I succeeded his father Darius I as king of Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes I followed his father Darius the Great on the Persian throne in 486 BC.

clue.text: Become liable to get cold in one jog around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the cold letter within the one-and-jog combination
around means the run word is turned back to front

parts.note: to jog is to run gently
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A jogger risks catching a chill when going out for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns RUN into NUR; I + NUR gives INUR, and 'in' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it on oneself, becoming liable to it.

clue.text: Slow Persians' leader captured by current enemy of his?

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: captured by means the leading letter is held inside the following pieces

parts.note: a Mede, from ancient Media, was a neighbour and rival of the Persians

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Persians' commander, seized by a rival, has his progress held up.
explanation.walkthrough: P (first of Persians) goes inside I + MEDE. 'his' points back to the Persian leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to slow or obstruct progress, so as a verb it matches slow.

clue.text: Not at all red hot?

parts.note: a calm, unflustered person is the opposite of heated; and a green salad vegetable is famously cold rather than red and fiery

explanation.surface: Something that is in no way glowing hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone utterly calm and composed, never heated or flustered under pressure.

clue.text: List furniture that may be taken round

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties and who does them
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A list of furniture items that can be moved around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotatable can be turned on an axis, which is being taken round.

clue.text: Was Saul thus concealing attack?

indicators.note: concealing means the answer is held inside the clue's run of words

explanation.surface: A biblical question about whether Saul hid his violent attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across wAS SAUL Thus.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack on a person or a military position.

clue.text: Mutual understanding is left after strike

indicators.note: after puts the word for left following the word for strike

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
port is the nautical left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Industrial relations break down: left-wing workers come out after a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship in which people understand each other well.

clue.text: Something useful, like radio

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a radio is a wireless set

explanation.surface: A radio is a handy thing to have around.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a valuable or useful thing or quality, like a skill that helps.

clue.text: Unstably drove crude boat which shows lack of balance

indicators.note: unstably signals the letters are shaken into a different order

parts.note: a raft is a rough, simple vessel

explanation.surface: Someone sailed a rickety vessel and kept losing their footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unstably' rearranges DROVE into OVERD, then RAFT. 'balance' is the bank balance, not physical steadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is a deficit on a bank account, showing that funds are missing.

clue.text: Place that's relaxing and making one happy

parts.note: PL is the street-name abbreviation for place
easing means loosening or relaxing

explanation.surface: A calm, restful spot that leaves visitors content.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pleasing gives satisfaction or enjoyment, cheering a person up.

clue.text: Beg in the name of god?

indicators.note: name of god means the god's name, so the god comes before the name

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Someone pleads in a holy name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link. In American English to panhandle is to beg in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To panhandle is an American word for begging from passers-by in public places.

clue.text: Shoal with black fish

parts.note: a shoal, a shallow area, can be a sandbar
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A school of dark fish swims by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoal' suggests a group of fish, but here it is a sandbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb, or barbel, is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Ability to feel heartless conjunction of words

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of that word is taken out

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling or sensation

explanation.surface: Words joined together without any feeling behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle I of SENTIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentence is a set of words joined into a complete grammatical statement.

clue.text: What's sweet way of behaving with girls?

parts.note: MO is short for modus operandi, a habitual way of doing things
lasses are girls, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A question about charming conduct toward young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is a thick, dark, sweet syrup produced when sugar is refined.

clue.text: Scientist forgetting old name for creature

indicators.note: forgetting means those letters are left out of the scientist

parts.note: Isaac Newton was the great English physicist

explanation.surface: A researcher keeps forgetting what an animal used to be called.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, so it is one example of a creature.

clue.text: Firm turning out our steel

indicators.note: turning out signals the letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A steelworks boasts of its sturdy product.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means determined and unwavering, so it shares the sense of firm resolve.

clue.text: Monks following bishop's line

indicators.note: following puts the monks word after the bishop letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a religious order is a community of monks

explanation.surface: Monks file in behind their bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is a boundary line dividing two areas or countries.

clue.text: Urgent court command

parts.note: dire means urgent, as in dire need

explanation.surface: A judge issues a pressing order from the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to command or order someone to do something.

clue.text: One studying bodies a military alliance overlooked in reporting

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization

indicators.note: in reporting means the word is spoken and we take its sound

parts.note: missed means overlooked

explanation.surface: A forensic expert misses a defence pact in their report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reporting' turns MISSED into its spoken twin MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist is a scientist who studies the structure of human or animal bodies.

clue.text: Sharp note during service

indicators.note: during places the note inside the service word

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
ut is the old name for the note now called do in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A high note rings out in a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church, but it is a tennis serve. UT is the old name of the first sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means sharp, whether of pain, angles, hearing or a keen mind.

clue.text: Fellow that is climbing mountain

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upward, so they are turned around

parts.note: Reg is a man's name, standing for any fellow
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A man is climbing a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns REG + IE (REGIE) into EIGER, the Swiss Alpine peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eiger is a famous Swiss Alpine peak known for its notorious north face.

clue.text: After key victory by duke, the French become weaker

parts.note: D is a musical key
a win is a victory
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Following a decisive win, the French duke's power begins to wane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'by' just join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to diminish gradually, growing smaller or less strong.

clue.text: Be old nag's supply? It might

definitions.text: Be old nag's supply? It might

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: A horse feed bag might hold an old nag's supply of oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as an adverb, in a supple manner, and rearranges BE + O + NAGS. Read whole, the clue also describes the feed bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosebag holds a horse's ration of feed, hung around its head.

clue.text: Composer's fury over rival's finale being included

indicators.note: being included means that letter goes inside the turned word
over means the fury word is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: rage is fury

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A composer flies into a jealous fury at a rival's concluding movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RAGE into EGAR; the L from 'rival's finale' goes inside. Edward Elgar was the English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Money dealer's time to back out of firm

indicators.note: out of here means the back word sits outside, enclosing the firm word

parts.note: the rear is the back
sure means firm or steady

explanation.surface: A banker's moment to withdraw from the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is read as 'outside', so the back word encloses the firm word rather than leaving it.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of an organisation, so is a handler of money.
